relations.relationship: Uses an explicit counterfactual about British nonintervention in 1914 to contest an inevitable-war narrative.
relations.evidence_note: Own 2007 interview answers on alternative futures and The Pity of War. His judgment that a German victory would have been tolerable remains disputed testimony, not this graph’s endorsed conclusion or a current strategic recommendation.

relations.relationship: Argues that causal explanations should state plausible alternative outcomes and preserve contemporaries’ uncertainty.
relations.evidence_note: Own answers to the causation, scientific-method and counterfactual questions. A methodological proposal about explanation, not proof that counterfactuals can be experimentally tested or that every imagined alternative is plausible.
